plan.chapterName: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e, chapter 1: Prerequisites
plan.contextChunk: This figure is a plain black line drawing of a right circular cylinder viewed in perspective from slightly above. The top face is rendered as a complete ellipse; the bottom is a partial ellipse whose far arc is omitted, and the two are joined by straight vertical lines at the left and right silhouette edges, so the solid reads as opaque. A horizontal arrow begins at the center of the top ellipse and points to the right until it touches the rim, with the italic label r sitting just above its shaft. Outside the body of the cylinder, to the right, a vertical double-headed arrow reaches from the level of the top rim down to the level of the bottom rim and is labeled h. There is no shading, no coordinate frame, and no numerical scale anywhere in the drawing. The two arrows isolate the only two measurements the solid requires, one running across the circular cross-section and one running along the axis. The picture accompanies the surface-area formula S = 2 pi r (r + h), fixing which distance the symbol r stands for and which the symbol h stands for.

elements: right circular cylinder with opaque white body
top circular cap drawn as a full ellipse
bottom cap drawn as a partial ellipse (far arc hidden, near arc visible)
two vertical silhouette edges connecting top and bottom caps
horizontal radius arrow from top-center to the right rim, labeled r
vertical double-headed height arrow outside the cylinder on the right, spanning top-rim to bottom-rim level, labeled h
net view: two flat circles of radius r (top and bottom caps) plus a rectangle of width 2*pi*r and height h

interactions.label: Radius r
interactions.teaches: Changing r widens the caps and the circumference simultaneously — r appears in both the cap area (pi r^2) and the lateral wrap (2 pi r h) of S = 2 pi r(r + h)

interactions.label: Height h
interactions.teaches: Changing h stretches the cylinder without touching the caps — h contributes only to the lateral surface term 2 pi r h

interactions.label: View
interactions.teaches: Unrolling the surface into two circles of radius r plus a rectangle of width 2 pi r and height h shows exactly where each term of S = 2 pi r(r + h) comes from

demo_steps.title: Identify r and h
demo_steps.narration: The default solid shows the radius arrow spanning the top cap and the height arrow spanning the side — the only two measurements the formula needs.

demo_steps.title: Stretch the height
demo_steps.narration: Increase h: the cylinder elongates but the caps stay the same size. Only the lateral area grows.

demo_steps.title: Widen the radius
demo_steps.narration: Increase r: both the caps and the wrap-around grow, since r feeds both terms of the formula.

demo_steps.title: Unroll to the net
demo_steps.narration: Switch to the net: two circles of area pi r^2 each plus a rectangle 2 pi r wide and h tall — the visual proof of S = 2 pi r(r + h).

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Cylinder: radius r (world units, default 1.2), height h (default 2.0), axis vertical along +Y, centered at origin. Rendered as opaque white surfaces with black outline strokes (like the source line drawing): top cap full ellipse, bottom cap only the front half of its rim visible, two vertical silhouette edges. Radius arrow: black horizontal arrow from axis center to right rim at top-cap level, label 'r' above. Height arrow: black vertical double-headed arrow offset ~0.6 units to the right of the cylinder silhouette, spanning the full height, label 'h' beside its midpoint. Net view: two flat circles radius r (one above, one below or beside) plus a rectangle exactly 2*pi*r wide and h tall, laid flat facing camera. Colors: white fill #ffffff, black lines #000000, labels italic black. No shading, no axes, no scale marks.
interactionPlan.notes: Use CylinderGeometry with open edges plus torus/ellipse rim strokes for the hand-drawn outline look, or simply white material with black EdgesGeometry. In net view use flat CircleGeometry and PlaneGeometry with black borders, and add dimension labels '2*pi*r' under the rectangle's width and 'h' beside its height. Update all geometry (caps, side, rim curves, arrows, net rectangle width) reactively on each slider change. Arrows should rescale with the cylinder.

A right circular cylinder with radius r and height h has the surface area S (in square units) given by the formula S=2πr(r+h). See the figure. Find the surface area of a cylinder with radius 6 in. and height 9 in. Leave the answer in terms of π.

Right circular cylinder

A right circular cylinder with an arrow extending from the center of the top circle outward to the edge, labeled: r. Another arrow beside the image going from top to bottom, labeled: h.
